structure: Part 8 of 16, Arrival, transit countries and transporter selection. Mined all 6 traces this part names, every action of each, from transport-and-arrival.fit.spec.js (read for test titles only): (1) arrival details › air and sea skip transit countries (64 actions, 0 errors); (2) arrival details › means of transport is the one required answer (105 actions, 0 errors, drives the error state); (3) transit countries › add and remove the countries the consignment travels through (103 actions); (4) transporter details › select a transporter from the list (85 actions); (5) transporter details › the legacy transport-details path redirects to the transporter page (65 actions); (6) transporter details › transporter is optional to proceed (66 actions). Every trace sets up the notification the same way (notification type live animals, origin France, chicken commodity, Internal market / Breeding, 100 animals) before navigating straight to /design-release-2.1/arrival-details; that set-up belongs to earlier parts and is not claimed here. Pages in journey order, all under /design-release-2.1/: (a) arrival-details, 'Arrival details', caption 'Transport and arrival', always shown; snapshot pointers: trace 1 action 44, trace 2 action 66 (error state), trace 6 action 46. (b) transit-countries, 'Which countries will the consignment travel through?', caption 'Movement', conditional: reached after Rail (trace 2 action 92) or Road (trace 3), and guarded with a redirect to the hub when means is Air (trace 1 action 50-51); pointers trace 3 actions 55, 70, 77, 88. (c) transporter, 'Transporter details', caption 'Transport and arrival', reached from arrival details after Air or from transit countries; pointers trace 4 action 60, trace 5 action 52. (d) the legacy /transport-details path, a 302 to /transporter (trace 5 request 319). Onward pages seen only as landing points: upload-documents ('Upload documents', trace 4 action 72, trace 6 action 53) and notification-hub ('Overview', trace 1 action 51). Integrations: the network logs show only same-origin prototype page GETs and form POSTs (bodies read for arrival-details, transit-countries, transporter); the port list (205 entries) is inlined in the arrival page HTML, the transit country list (41 entries) is inlined as application/json in the transit page, and the 8 transporters are server-rendered rows; no reference-data or API call fired. Adding a new transporter (/transporter/add) is part 9's and is claimed here only as the link that leads to it. Surfaces the traces never reached (Sea route, blank transit submit, date validation, transporter search, View details, Save and return, Cancel) are recorded as gaps.
